items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: Fats Domino and them had been the studio or Dave Bartholomew and rock was beginning to really go. ... We were the second tier.

ctx.x: That formula was not going to work.

That’s right. And that’s what I tell all the young kids now. You know they say, “I want to be a musician, I’m going to New York, I’m going to do this.” I say, “man, get your degree so at least you can have something to fall back on.” And I wasn’t never in the thing of being a professional musician, my whole thing was teaching and all the gigs and things on the side. And I had too many of them on the side because after I got out of school I started playing in rhythm & blues. Rock & roll was just coming on, so I…
